How do different laser types work?
There are two main types of laser (optical and IR):
Optical laser (optic): Optical lasers include CO2, Nd:YAG, CW, solid state and fiber lasers. They use a solid medium (typically crystal, glass or diamond) to amplify laser light.
IR laser (Infrared): IR lasers include CW, CO2, Nd:glass, Nd:YAG, solid state, solid oxide and fiber lasers. The laser is "tuned" to work in a specific wavelength of the infrared spectrum (which is invisible to the human eye).
Both types of laser can be used to measure distance, but the wavelengths they produce allow them to be used for slightly different purposes.
Optical lasers are generally used to measure shorter distances (up to about 10 meters) and to create highly detailed 3D maps of the scanned area. They can be used in various industries, such as construction, manufacturing, automotive and aerospace.
Infrared lasers are generally used to measure longer distances (up to around 500 meters), and are typically used in applications where accuracy or precision is not as critical.
The wavelength of an IR laser in particular can allow it to penetrate certain materials that would interfere with an optical laser.
Overall, both types of laser have their own advantages and limitations, and the choice of which one to use will depend on the specific application and requirements.
Are laser distance measurement devices reliable?
The accuracy of laser distance measurement devices depends on several factors, such as ambient light conditions, the quality of the laser sensor, and the precision of the measurements taken. Additionally, it is important to take into consideration any potential sources of error that may affect the measurements. By following these steps, it is possible to achieve reliable and consistent results when using laser distance measurement devices.
